column_map.OM: OM percent, and Total carbon = OM / 1.724

absent_at_source.EC: the workbook has no electrical conductivity column; EC is written empty so the table keeps the project's five inputs

derived_target.why: the workbook measures organic matter, not carbon; the pipeline targets total carbon, so a conversion is required or the dataset has no target at all
derived_target.limitation: OM/1.724 estimates organic carbon; AfSIS total carbon includes any inorganic fraction, so the two scales are assumed equal here, not proved equal
derived_target.support: carbonate is not expected below about pH 6.5; the count of samples above that line is reported in quality.ph
derived_target.traceability: carbon_source column repeats the conversion per row

grouping: SSN, one row per sample. SiteName (demo host) is reported but is deliberately not named SiteID: clean() deduplicates on [group key, lab], so a coarser key would keep one row per farm and discard the rest.
cleaning: nothing imputed, aggregated or clamped here; out-of-bounds values are left for afsis_data.clean() to report

repeated_records.note: the ten OM..Silt columns repeat verbatim in blocks of 16-23 rows while pH varies, so they carry a filled-down value rather than a per-farm measurement. record_pattern names each distinct vector: identical rows must share a fold, or a cross-validated score measures recall of that table instead of prediction.

target_note: not measured: estimated from organic matter, see derived_target

attribution.credit: 2025 farmer demonstration soils; the agronomists who collected them are named in the Georeferences table
attribution.warning: afsis_experiment.py labels any root without a synthetic marker as 'afsis_real' and prints the AfSIS credit, which is the wrong attribution for this dataset. Until a run can be told this source kind, a bundle produced from this root must not be cited.

run_note: --drop-features EC is required: EC is absent at source, so a five-feature model cannot score or train on these rows
known_defect: the repeated chemistry blocks in quality.repeated_records inflate any cross-validated score computed from this root, because identical rows are split across folds; the workbook needs correcting, or the run needs to group on record_pattern, before a score from it means anything
